Title: Annual Leave Policy – US
Policy ID: HR-POL-001
Owner: Employee Relations Manager
Department: Human Resources
Effective Date: 2021-06-01
Version: 1.0
Status: active
Applicable Regions: US
Approval Body: HR Committee

1. Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to define the entitlements and procedures for Annual Leave at HYTech Solutions, ensuring consistency, fairness, and compliance with applicable regional employment regulations.
This policy establishes the standards and requirements for leave at HYTech Solutions.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all employees in US.
All covered employees must comply with this policy from the effective date forward.
Contractors and temporary staff are subject to equivalent requirements unless explicitly exempted.

3. Eligibility
Eligibility is determined by employment type, tenure, and region as specified below.
- Minimum tenure: 3 months
- Employee classification: all
- Applicable regions: US
- Employees in US are subject to local statutory minimums that may exceed the values stated in Section 4.

4. Policy Statement
All eligible HYTech Solutions employees are entitled to a standard entitlement of 15 business days per calendar year. This entitlement is subject to the eligibility criteria and approval procedures described in this policy.
The standard entitlement under this policy is 15 business days per calendar year.
All entitlements are subject to the eligibility criteria in Section 3 and the approval process in Section 5.

5. Procedure
1. Submit a leave request through HYPortal at least 3 business days before the intended start date.
2. Obtain line manager approval within HYPortal.
3. HR Operations will confirm the leave balance deduction within 2 business days.
4. Upon return, update your attendance record in HYPortal.

6. Exceptions
The following exceptions apply to the standard policy:
The following exceptions to the standard policy are recognised:
- Contractors engaged through third-party agencies are not eligible unless explicitly stated in the engagement contract.
- Interns on fixed-term agreements of less than six months are not eligible for this entitlement.
Exceptions must be documented and retained by the HR Operations team for a minimum of 7 years.

7. Manager Responsibilities
Managers are responsible for:
- Approving requests within 5 business days
- Ensuring compliance with this policy across their direct reports
- Escalating non-standard cases to the HR Operations Lead before approval
- Maintaining accurate records in the HR information system

8. Employee Responsibilities
Employees must:
- Submit requests via the HR self-service portal at least 3 business days in advance
- Obtain written approval from their direct manager before confirming arrangements
- Notify the HR Operations Lead if circumstances change after approval

9. Escalation
Unresolved queries should be directed to the HR Operations Lead.
Escalations must be submitted in writing and acknowledged within 2 business days.
Disputes that cannot be resolved within 10 business days will be referred to the HR Committee.

10. Revision History
| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0 | 2021-05-02 | Employee Relations Manager | Initial release |

body:
Title: Lodging Expense Policy – US (USD)
Policy ID: TRV-POL-001
Owner: Security Engineer
Department: Finance
Effective Date: 2021-09-01
Version: 1.0
Status: active
Currency: USD
Expense Type: lodging
Approval Required: False

1. Purpose
This policy defines the reimbursement rules and spending limits for lodging expenses
incurred by HYTech Solutions employees on approved business activities.
All claims must be submitted within 30 calendar days of the expense date.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all HYTech Solutions employees and contractors who incur lodging
expenses in the course of authorised business travel or remote work activities.
Expenses claimed in currencies other than USD will be converted at the corporate rate
on the date of expenditure.

3. Spending Limits
The following table specifies the maximum reimbursable amounts per lodging event
by employee role and region. Amounts are in USD.

| Expense Type | Role | Region | Limit (USD) | Approval Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lodging | Employee | US | 150 | No |
| Lodging | Manager | US | 200 | No |
| Lodging | Executive | US | 350 | No |
| Lodging | Sales | US | 200 | No |
| Lodging | Engineer | US | 150 | No |

4. Receipt Requirements
Receipts are mandatory for all expenses exceeding 50 USD.
Itemised receipts must be uploaded via the Expense Management Portal within 30 days.
Missing receipts for amounts above the threshold will result in claim rejection.
Digital receipts (PDF, email confirmation) are accepted in lieu of physical receipts.

5. Approval Process
lodging expenses below the spending limit do not require pre-approval.
Expenses above the spending limit require manager approval before reimbursement is processed.

6. Exceptions
Expenses that exceed the stated limits may be approved in exceptional circumstances:
- Client entertainment events with documented business justification
- Emergency travel or accommodation required due to safety concerns
- Events in high-cost locations where standard limits are insufficient (requires Finance Lead sign-off)
Exceptions must be approved in writing before the expense is incurred where reasonably practicable.

7. Reimbursement Timeline
Approved claims are reimbursed within 30 calendar days of approval.
Claims submitted after the 30-day window may be rejected at the discretion
of the Finance Lead. Queries regarding pending claims should be directed to Finance Controller.

8. Non-Reimbursable Expenses
The following lodging expenses are not reimbursable under any circumstances:
- Hotel room service and minibar charges
- Personal laundry or dry-cleaning services
- In-room entertainment not required for business

9. Policy Compliance and Audit
The Finance Operations team conducts quarterly audits of lodging expense claims.
Policy violations may result in repayment obligations and disciplinary action.
All records are retained for 7 years in compliance with statutory requirements.

10. Revision History
| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0 | 2021-08-02 | Security Engineer | Initial release |

All claims must be submitted within 30 calendar days of the expense date.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all HYTech Solutions employees and contractors who incur lodging
expenses in the course of authorised business travel or remote work activities.
Expenses claimed in currencies other than EUR will be converted at the corporate rate
on the date of expenditure.

3. Spending Limits
The following table specifies the maximum reimbursable amounts per lodging event
by employee role and region. Amounts are in EUR.

| Expense Type | Role | Region | Limit (EUR) | Approval Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lodging | Employee | EU | 120 | No |
| Lodging | Manager | EU | 160 | No |
| Lodging | Executive | EU | 280 | No |
| Lodging | Sales | EU | 160 | No |
| Lodging | Engineer | EU | 120 | No |

4. Receipt Requirements
Receipts are mandatory for all expenses exceeding 40 EUR.
Itemised receipts must be uploaded via the Expense Management Portal within 30 days.
Missing receipts for amounts above the threshold will result in claim rejection.
Digital receipts (PDF, email confirmation) are accepted in lieu of physical receipts.

5. Approval Process
lodging expenses below the spending limit do not require pre-approval.
Expenses above the spending limit require manager approval before reimbursement is processed.

6. Exceptions
Expenses that exceed the stated limits may be approved in exceptional circumstances:
- Client entertainment events with documented business justification
- Emergency travel or accommodation required due to safety concerns
- Events in high-cost locations where standard limits are insufficient (requires Finance Lead sign-off)
Exceptions must be approved in writing before the expense is incurred where reasonably practicable.

7. Reimbursement Timeline
Approved claims are reimbursed within 30 calendar days of approval.
Claims submitted after the 30-day window may be rejected at the discretion
of the Finance Lead. Queries regarding pending claims should be directed to Finance Controller.

8. Non-Reimbursable Expenses
The following lodging expenses are not reimbursable under any circumstances:
- Hotel room service and minibar charges
- Personal laundry or dry-cleaning services
- In-room entertainment not required for business

9. Policy Compliance and Audit
The Finance Operations team conducts quarterly audits of lodging expense claims.
Policy violations may result in repayment obligations and disciplinary action.
All records are retained for 7 years in compliance with statutory requirements.

1. Purpose
This policy defines the reimbursement rules and spending limits for meals expenses
incurred by HYTech Solutions employees on approved business activities.
All claims must be submitted within 30 calendar days of the expense date.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all HYTech Solutions employees and contractors who incur meals
expenses in the course of authorised business travel or remote work activities.

by employee role and region. Amounts are in USD.

| Expense Type | Role | Region | Limit (USD) | Approval Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Meals | Employee | US | 60 | No |
| Meals | Manager | US | 80 | No |
| Meals | Executive | US | 120 | No |
| Meals | Sales | US | 100 | No |
| Meals | Engineer | US | 60 | No |

4. Receipt Requirements
Receipts are mandatory for all expenses exceeding 25 USD.
Itemised receipts must be uploaded via the Expense Management Portal within 30 days.
Missing receipts for amounts above the threshold will result in claim rejection.
Digital receipts (PDF, email confirmation) are accepted in lieu of physical receipts.

5. Approval Process
meals expenses below the spending limit do not require pre-approval.

- Events in high-cost locations where standard limits are insufficient (requires Finance Lead sign-off)

Version: 1.2
Status: active
Currency: KRW
Expense Type: meals
Approval Required: False

1. Purpose
This policy defines the reimbursement rules and spending limits for meals expenses
incurred by HYTech Solutions employees on approved business activities.
All claims must be submitted within 30 calendar days of the expense date.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all HYTech Solutions employees and contractors who incur meals
expenses in the course of authorised business travel or remote work activities.
Expenses claimed in currencies other than KRW will be converted at the corporate rate
on the date of expenditure.

3. Spending Limits
The following table specifies the maximum reimbursable amounts per meals event
by employee role and region. Amounts are in KRW.

| Expense Type | Role | Region | Limit (KRW) | Approval Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Meals | Employee | KR | 40000 | No |
| Meals | Manager | KR | 60000 | No |
| Meals | Executive | KR | 100000 | No |
| Meals | Sales | KR | 70000 | No |
| Meals | Engineer | KR | 40000 | No |

4. Receipt Requirements
Receipts are mandatory for all expenses exceeding 20000 KRW.
Itemised receipts must be uploaded via the Expense Management Portal within 30 days.
Missing receipts for amounts above the threshold will result in claim rejection.
Digital receipts (PDF, email confirmation) are accepted in lieu of physical receipts.

5. Approval Process
meals expenses below the spending limit do not require pre-approval.
Expenses above the spending limit require manager approval before reimbursement is processed.

6. Exceptions
Expenses that exceed the stated limits may be approved in exceptional circumstances:
- Client entertainment events with documented business justification
- Emergency travel or accommodation required due to safety concerns
- Events in high-cost locations where standard limits are insufficient (requires Finance Lead sign-off)
Exceptions must be approved in writing before the expense is incurred where reasonably practicable.

7. Reimbursement Timeline
Approved claims are reimbursed within 30 calendar days of approval.
Claims submitted after the 30-day window may be rejected at the discretion
of the Finance Lead. Queries regarding pending claims should be directed to Finance Controller.

8. Non-Reimbursable Expenses
The following meals expenses are not reimbursable under any circumstances:
- Alcohol purchased for personal consumption
- Meals for non-HYTech guests not on approved list
- Delivery service fees exceeding 15% of the meal cost

9. Policy Compliance and Audit
The Finance Operations team conducts quarterly audits of meals expense claims.
Policy violations may result in repayment obligations and disciplinary action.
All records are retained for 7 years in compliance with statutory requirements.

10. Revision History
| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0 | 2022-07-28 | Security Engineer | Initial release |

This policy defines the reimbursement rules and spending limits for airfare expenses
incurred by HYTech Solutions employees on approved business activities.

This policy applies to all HYTech Solutions employees and contractors who incur airfare
expenses in the course of authorised business travel or remote work activities.

on the date of expenditure.

| Airfare | Manager | US | 1200 | Yes |
| Airfare | Executive | US | 3000 | Yes |
| Airfare | Sales | US | 1500 | Yes |
| Airfare | Engineer | US | 1000 | Yes |

4. Receipt Requirements
Receipts are mandatory for all expenses exceeding 100 USD.
Itemised receipts must be uploaded via the Expense Management Portal within 30 days.
Missing receipts for amounts above the threshold will result in claim rejection.

All airfare expenses require pre-approval from the direct manager before commitment.

- Emergency travel or accommodation required due to safety concerns
- Events in high-cost locations where standard limits are insufficient (requires Finance Lead sign-off)

- Travel insurance not pre-approved by Finance
- Airport lounge access (except for Executive role-holders)

The Finance Operations team conducts quarterly audits of airfare expense claims.

All records are retained for 7 years in compliance with statutory requirements.

1. Purpose
This policy defines the reimbursement rules and spending limits for ground transport expenses
incurred by HYTech Solutions employees on approved business activities.
All claims must be submitted within 30 calendar days of the expense date.

This policy applies to all HYTech Solutions employees and contractors who incur ground transport
expenses in the course of authorised business travel or remote work activities.

on the date of expenditure.

by employee role and region. Amounts are in USD.

| Ground Transport | Manager | US | 75 | No |
| Ground Transport | Executive | US | 120 | No |
| Ground Transport | Sales | US | 75 | No |
| Ground Transport | Engineer | US | 50 | No |

4. Receipt Requirements
Receipts are mandatory for all expenses exceeding 20 USD.
Itemised receipts must be uploaded via the Expense Management Portal within 30 days.
Missing receipts for amounts above the threshold will result in claim rejection.
Digital receipts (PDF, email confirmation) are accepted in lieu of physical receipts.

ground transport expenses below the spending limit do not require pre-approval.

Title: Ground Transport Expense Policy – KR (KRW)
Policy ID: TRV-POL-012
Owner: Platform Architect
Department: Finance
Effective Date: 2023-06-23
Version: 1.3
Status: active
Currency: KRW
Expense Type: ground transport
Approval Required: False

1. Purpose
This policy defines the reimbursement rules and spending limits for ground transport expenses
incurred by HYTech Solutions employees on approved business activities.
All claims must be submitted within 30 calendar days of the expense date.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all HYTech Solutions employees and contractors who incur ground transport
expenses in the course of authorised business travel or remote work activities.
Expenses claimed in currencies other than KRW will be converted at the corporate rate
on the date of expenditure.

3. Spending Limits
The following table specifies the maximum reimbursable amounts per ground transport event
by employee role and region. Amounts are in KRW.

| Expense Type | Role | Region | Limit (KRW) | Approval Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ground Transport | Employee | KR | 30000 | No |
| Ground Transport | Manager | KR | 50000 | No |
| Ground Transport | Executive | KR | 80000 | No |
| Ground Transport | Sales | KR | 50000 | No |
| Ground Transport | Engineer | KR | 30000 | No |

4. Receipt Requirements
Receipts are mandatory for all expenses exceeding 10000 KRW.
Itemised receipts must be uploaded via the Expense Management Portal within 30 days.
Missing receipts for amounts above the threshold will result in claim rejection.
Digital receipts (PDF, email confirmation) are accepted in lieu of physical receipts.

5. Approval Process
ground transport expenses below the spending limit do not require pre-approval.
Expenses above the spending limit require manager approval before reimbursement is processed.

6. Exceptions
Expenses that exceed the stated limits may be approved in exceptional circumstances:
- Client entertainment events with documented business justification
- Emergency travel or accommodation required due to safety concerns
- Events in high-cost locations where standard limits are insufficient (requires Finance Lead sign-off)
Exceptions must be approved in writing before the expense is incurred where reasonably practicable.

7. Reimbursement Timeline
Approved claims are reimbursed within 30 calendar days of approval.
Claims submitted after the 30-day window may be rejected at the discretion
of the Finance Lead. Queries regarding pending claims should be directed to Finance Controller.

8. Non-Reimbursable Expenses
The following ground transport expenses are not reimbursable under any circumstances:
- Tolls for personal detours unrelated to the business destination
- Parking fines or traffic violations
- Car rental upgrade costs beyond the standard category

9. Policy Compliance and Audit
The Finance Operations team conducts quarterly audits of ground transport expense claims.
Policy violations may result in repayment obligations and disciplinary action.
All records are retained for 7 years in compliance with statutory requirements.

10. Revision History
| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |

| 1.3 | 2023-06-23 | Finance Controller | Updated spending limits for KRW region |

body:
Title: Multi-Factor Authentication Enforcement
Policy ID: SEC-POL-001
Owner: Chief Information Security Officer
Department: Security
Effective Date: 2021-03-01
Version: 1.0
Status: active
Control Family: Access Control
Risk Level: critical
Control IDs: HY-AC-01, HY-AC-02
Review Frequency: 90 days

1. Purpose
This policy establishes mandatory controls for the Access Control security domain at HYTech Solutions.
The controls described herein are required to maintain the organisation's security posture and
comply with applicable regulatory frameworks.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all systems, personnel, and third-party integrations operating within
the HYTech Solutions environment that fall under the Access Control control domain.
Enforcement is the responsibility of the Engineering Manager.

3. Control Requirements
The following controls are mandated under this policy:

| Control ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HY-AC-01 | All employees must enroll in MFA within 5 business days of account creation. | Active |
| HY-AC-02 | MFA must use TOTP or hardware security keys; SMS-based MFA is prohibited. | Active |

All mandatory requirements must be implemented without exception unless a formal waiver has
been granted by the Chief Information Security Officer.

4. Risk Classification
This policy addresses critical risk events in the Access Control domain.
Risk events in this category have the following characteristics:
- Likelihood: Highly likely without mandatory controls
- Potential impact: Catastrophic — potential for data breach, regulatory penalty, or service outage
- Detection difficulty: Difficult — may go undetected without dedicated monitoring

5. Incident Response and Escalation
In the event of a policy violation or security incident, the following escalation timeline applies:

| Risk Level | Escalation Deadline | Primary Contact | Secondary Contact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | 1 hour | Engineering Manager | Chief Information Security Officer |
| High | 4 hours | Engineering Manager | Security Operations Lead |
| Medium | 24 hours | Engineering Manager | Security Operations Lead |
| Low | 3 business days | Engineering Manager | Security Operations Lead |

All incidents must be logged in the Security Incident Tracking System within the above deadlines.

6. Mandatory Requirements
The following actions are required for compliance with control(s) HY-AC-01, HY-AC-02:
- All employees must enroll in MFA within 5 business days of account creation.
- MFA must use TOTP or hardware security keys; SMS-based MFA is prohibited.
- Service accounts must use certificate-based authentication or service tokens.
- MFA bypass is prohibited without CISO approval.

7. Prohibited Actions
The following actions are explicitly prohibited under this policy:
- Sharing MFA codes or recovery codes with any other person.
- Disabling MFA on any production system without CISO written approval.
- Using SMS as a sole MFA factor for accounts with privileged access.

8. Exceptions
No exceptions are permitted for critical risk controls in the Access Control domain.
All requirements in Section 6 are non-negotiable.

9. Audit and Compliance
The Security Operations team conducts reviews of this policy's compliance every 90 days.
Non-compliance identified during audit must be remediated within 3 business days.
Evidence of compliance must be documented and available for audit at all times.

10. Revision History
| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0 | 2020-12-31 | Chief Information Security Officer | Initial release |

1. Purpose
This policy establishes mandatory controls for the Access Control security domain at HYTech Solutions.
The controls described herein are required to maintain the organisation's security posture and
comply with applicable regulatory frameworks.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all systems, personnel, and third-party integrations operating within
the HYTech Solutions environment that fall under the Access Control control domain.
Enforcement is the responsibility of the Security Engineer.

3. Control Requirements
The following controls are mandated under this policy:

| Control ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HY-AC-07 | Access reviews must be completed quarterly for all production systems. | Active |
| HY-AC-08 | Access for terminated employees must be revoked within 1 business day. | Active |

All mandatory requirements must be implemented without exception unless a formal waiver has
been granted by the Chief Information Security Officer.

4. Risk Classification
This policy addresses medium risk events in the Access Control domain.
Risk events in this category have the following characteristics:

- Potential impact: Moderate — limited data exposure or short-term service degradation
- Detection difficulty: Easy — typically surfaced by routine log review

- Storing Restricted data in unencrypted cloud storage.

Title: Security Incident Classification and Response
Policy ID: SEC-POL-011
Owner: Chief Information Security Officer
Department: Security
Effective Date: 2022-07-14
Version: 1.0
Status: active
Control Family: Incident Response
Risk Level: critical
Control IDs: HY-IR-01, HY-IR-02
Review Frequency: 90 days

1. Purpose
This policy establishes mandatory controls for the Incident Response security domain at HYTech Solutions.
The controls described herein are required to maintain the organisation's security posture and
comply with applicable regulatory frameworks.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all systems, personnel, and third-party integrations operating within
the HYTech Solutions environment that fall under the Incident Response control domain.
Enforcement is the responsibility of the Security Engineer.

3. Control Requirements
The following controls are mandated under this policy:

| Control ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HY-IR-01 | All security incidents must be reported to the Security team within 1 hour of discovery. | Active |
| HY-IR-02 | Critical incidents require immediate escalation to CISO and Engineering VP. | Active |

All mandatory requirements must be implemented without exception unless a formal waiver has
been granted by the Chief Information Security Officer.

4. Risk Classification
This policy addresses critical risk events in the Incident Response domain.
Risk events in this category have the following characteristics:
- Likelihood: Highly likely without mandatory controls
- Potential impact: Catastrophic — potential for data breach, regulatory penalty, or service outage
- Detection difficulty: Difficult — may go undetected without dedicated monitoring

5. Incident Response and Escalation
In the event of a policy violation or security incident, the following escalation timeline applies:

| Risk Level | Escalation Deadline | Primary Contact | Secondary Contact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | 1 hour | Security Engineer | Chief Information Security Officer |
| High | 4 hours | Security Engineer | Security Operations Lead |
| Medium | 24 hours | Security Engineer | Security Operations Lead |
| Low | 3 business days | Security Engineer | Security Operations Lead |

All incidents must be logged in the Security Incident Tracking System within the above deadlines.

6. Mandatory Requirements
The following actions are required for compliance with control(s) HY-IR-01, HY-IR-02:
- All security incidents must be reported to the Security team within 1 hour of discovery.
- Critical incidents require immediate escalation to CISO and Engineering VP.
- Incident severity must be classified using the defined severity matrix.
- Post-incident reviews must be completed within 5 business days for Severity 1 and 2 incidents.

7. Prohibited Actions
The following actions are explicitly prohibited under this policy:
- Investigating or remediating a security incident without informing the Security team.
- Disclosing incident details externally without CISO and Legal approval.

8. Exceptions
No exceptions are permitted for critical risk controls in the Incident Response domain.
All requirements in Section 6 are non-negotiable.

9. Audit and Compliance
The Security Operations team conducts reviews of this policy's compliance every 90 days.
Non-compliance identified during audit must be remediated within 3 business days.
Evidence of compliance must be documented and available for audit at all times.

10. Revision History
| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0 | 2022-05-15 | Chief Information Security Officer | Initial release |

This policy establishes mandatory controls for the Incident Response security domain at HYTech Solutions.

Owner: Chief Information Security Officer
Department: Security

Version: 1.2
Status: active
Control Family: Incident Response
Risk Level: high
Control IDs: HY-IR-05, HY-IR-06
Review Frequency: 180 days

1. Purpose
This policy establishes mandatory controls for the Incident Response security domain at HYTech Solutions.
The controls described herein are required to maintain the organisation's security posture and
comply with applicable regulatory frameworks.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all systems, personnel, and third-party integrations operating within
the HYTech Solutions environment that fall under the Incident Response control domain.
Enforcement is the responsibility of the Security Engineer.

3. Control Requirements
The following controls are mandated under this policy:

| Control ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HY-IR-05 | Digital evidence must be collected using approved forensic tools only. | Active |
| HY-IR-06 | Chain of custody must be documented for all evidence. | Active |

All mandatory requirements must be implemented without exception unless a formal waiver has
been granted by the Chief Information Security Officer.

4. Risk Classification
This policy addresses high risk events in the Incident Response domain.
Risk events in this category have the following characteristics:
- Likelihood: Likely if controls are absent
- Potential impact: Significant — possible data exposure or prolonged service disruption
- Detection difficulty: Moderate — detectable with standard SIEM alerting

5. Incident Response and Escalation
In the event of a policy violation or security incident, the following escalation timeline applies:

| Risk Level | Escalation Deadline | Primary Contact | Secondary Contact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | 1 hour | Security Engineer | Chief Information Security Officer |
| High | 4 hours | Security Engineer | Security Operations Lead |
| Medium | 24 hours | Security Engineer | Security Operations Lead |
| Low | 3 business days | Security Engineer | Security Operations Lead |

All incidents must be logged in the Security Incident Tracking System within the above deadlines.

6. Mandatory Requirements
The following actions are required for compliance with control(s) HY-IR-05, HY-IR-06:
- Digital evidence must be collected using approved forensic tools only.
- Chain of custody must be documented for all evidence.
- Systems under investigation must not be modified before evidence is collected.
- Forensic findings must be stored in the Security Evidence Repository for 3 years.

- Shutting down or reimaging systems under investigation without forensic evidence capture.
- Accessing evidence storage without documented authorisation.

following conditions:
- A documented business justification is provided
- Compensating controls are identified and implemented
- The exception is time-limited (maximum 30 days)
- The exception is reviewed at each 180-day review cycle

9. Audit and Compliance
The Security Operations team conducts reviews of this policy's compliance every 180 days.
Non-compliance identified during audit must be remediated within 7 business days.

| High | 4 hours | Engineering Manager | Security Operations Lead |
| Medium | 24 hours | Engineering Manager | Security Operations Lead |
| Low | 3 business days | Engineering Manager | Security Operations Lead |

All incidents must be logged in the Security Incident Tracking System within the above deadlines.

6. Mandatory Requirements
The following actions are required for compliance with control(s) HY-IR-09, HY-IR-10:
- All production systems must be scanned for vulnerabilities at least every 30 days.
- Critical vulnerabilities must be remediated within 7 days of discovery.
- High vulnerabilities must be remediated within 30 days.
- Vulnerability scan reports must be reviewed by the Security team within 5 business days.

7. Prohibited Actions
The following actions are explicitly prohibited under this policy:
- Deploying systems with known critical vulnerabilities to production.

Exceptions to this policy may be approved by the Chief Information Security Officer under the
following conditions:
- A documented business justification is provided
- Compensating controls are identified and implemented
- The exception is time-limited (maximum 180 days)
- The exception is reviewed at each 365-day review cycle

9. Audit and Compliance
The Security Operations team conducts reviews of this policy's compliance every 365 days.
Non-compliance identified during audit must be remediated within 90 business days.
Evidence of compliance must be documented and available for audit at all times.

Title: Endpoint Encryption Requirements
Policy ID: SEC-POL-016
Owner: Chief Information Security Officer
Department: IT Operations
Effective Date: 2023-03-21
Version: 1.0
Status: active
Control Family: Device Security
Risk Level: critical
Control IDs: HY-DS-01, HY-DS-02
Review Frequency: 90 days

1. Purpose
This policy establishes mandatory controls for the Device Security security domain at HYTech Solutions.
The controls described herein are required to maintain the organisation's security posture and
comply with applicable regulatory frameworks.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all systems, personnel, and third-party integrations operating within
the HYTech Solutions environment that fall under the Device Security control domain.
Enforcement is the responsibility of the Engineering Manager.

3. Control Requirements
The following controls are mandated under this policy:

| Control ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HY-DS-01 | All corporate laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled using BitLocker or FileVault. | Active |
| HY-DS-02 | Encryption keys must be escrowed in HYVault within 24 hours of device provisioning. | Active |

All mandatory requirements must be implemented without exception unless a formal waiver has
been granted by the Chief Information Security Officer.

4. Risk Classification
This policy addresses critical risk events in the Device Security domain.
Risk events in this category have the following characteristics:
- Likelihood: Highly likely without mandatory controls
- Potential impact: Catastrophic — potential for data breach, regulatory penalty, or service outage
- Detection difficulty: Difficult — may go undetected without dedicated monitoring

5. Incident Response and Escalation
In the event of a policy violation or security incident, the following escalation timeline applies:

| Risk Level | Escalation Deadline | Primary Contact | Secondary Contact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | 1 hour | Engineering Manager | Chief Information Security Officer |
| High | 4 hours | Engineering Manager | Security Operations Lead |
| Medium | 24 hours | Engineering Manager | Security Operations Lead |
| Low | 3 business days | Engineering Manager | Security Operations Lead |

All incidents must be logged in the Security Incident Tracking System within the above deadlines.

6. Mandatory Requirements
The following actions are required for compliance with control(s) HY-DS-01, HY-DS-02:
- All corporate laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled using BitLocker or FileVault.
- Encryption keys must be escrowed in HYVault within 24 hours of device provisioning.
- Unencrypted devices must not be used to access corporate systems.
- Encryption compliance must be verified monthly through HYPortal MDM.

7. Prohibited Actions
The following actions are explicitly prohibited under this policy:
- Disabling disk encryption on any corporate device.
- Using personal devices without MDM enrollment to access Confidential or Restricted data.

8. Exceptions
No exceptions are permitted for critical risk controls in the Device Security domain.
All requirements in Section 6 are non-negotiable.

9. Audit and Compliance
The Security Operations team conducts reviews of this policy's compliance every 90 days.
Non-compliance identified during audit must be remediated within 3 business days.
Evidence of compliance must be documented and available for audit at all times.

10. Revision History
| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0 | 2023-01-20 | Chief Information Security Officer | Initial release |

- `scope` (query, string): Optional: scope

Retrieve the JSON Web Key Set for verifying HYID-issued tokens.

Parameters:

### POST /api/v1/users
Create a new user account in the HYID directory.

- `email` (body/query, string, required): The email
- `display_name` (body/query, string, required): The display name
- `department` (body/query, string, required): The department
- `roles` (query, string): Optional: roles
- `region` (query, string): Optional: region

### DELETE /api/v1/users/{user_id}
Deactivate a user account and revoke all active sessions.

Parameters:
- `user_id` (body/query, string, required): The user id

This document describes the v1 API for the HYDeploy Release Management Service service.

Service: HYDeploy Release Management Service
Version: v3
Owner Team: Platform Engineering
Authentication: service token
Stability: experimental
Department: Platform Engineering
Effective Date: 2023-02-10

1. Overview
This document describes the v3 API for the HYDeploy Release Management Service service.
Automated deployment and release management service for HYTech Solutions applications, supporting blue-green deployments, canary releases, and rollback operations.
Base URL: https://api.hytech-solutions.internal/hydeploy/v3
Authentication method: service token
All requests must include the Authorization header with a valid token.

2. Authentication
Authentication uses service token. Refer to the HYTech Developer Portal for setup instructions.

3. Endpoints
### POST /api/v3/gates/{app_id}
Evaluate deployment gate conditions before proceeding to the next stage.

Parameters:
- `app_id` (body/query, string, required): The app id
- `gate_type` (body/query, string, required): The gate type
- `override_token` (query, string): Optional: override token

### GET /api/v3/artifacts
List available build artifacts for deployment.

Parameters:
- `app_id` (body/query, string, required): The app id
- `branch` (query, string): Optional: branch
- `status` (query, string): Optional: status
- `page` (query, string): Optional: page

### POST /api/v3/deployments/{deployment_id}/rollback
Roll back a failed or problematic deployment to the previous successful version.

Parameters:
- `deployment_id` (body/query, string, required): The deployment id
- `reason` (query, string): Optional: reason

### POST /api/v3/apps/{app_id}/promote
Promote a canary or staging deployment to full production traffic.

Parameters:
- `app_id` (body/query, string, required): The app id
- `deployment_id` (body/query, string, required): The deployment id
- `approval_token` (query, string): Optional: approval token

### GET /api/v3/apps/{app_id}/deployments
List all deployment history for a specific application.

Parameters:
- `app_id` (body/query, string, required): The app id
- `environment` (query, string): Optional: environment
- `status` (query, string): Optional: status
- `page` (query, string): Optional: page
- `page_size` (query, string): Optional: page size


4. Error Codes
The following error codes may be returned by the HYDeploy Release Management Service v3 API:

| Code | Message | Description | Recommended Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | Bad Request | Bad Request | Verify all required parameters are present. |
| 401 | Unauthorized | Unauthorized | Provide a valid service token in the Authorization header. |
| 403 | Forbidden | Forbidden | The requestor lacks the deploy permission for this application. |
| 404 | Not Found | Not Found | Verify the app_id or deployment_id is correct. |
| 409 | Conflict | Conflict | A deployment is already in progress for this application and environment. |
| 422 | Unprocessable Entity | Unprocessable Entity | Deployment failed gate validation; check gate conditions. |
| 429 | Too Many Requests | Too Many Requests | Reduce deployment frequency; maximum 10 concurrent deployments per app. |
| 500 | Internal Server Error | Internal Server Error | Retry after 60 seconds; contact Platform Engineering if unresolved. |
| 503 | Service Unavailable | Service Unavailable | HYDeploy service is undergoing maintenance; retry after 5 minutes. |

5. Rate Limits
The following rate limits apply to the HYDeploy Release Management Service v3 API:

| Tier | Requests per Minute | Burst Limit | Daily Quota |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | 100 | 150 | 10,000 |
| Standard | 1,000 | 1,500 | 100,000 |
| Enterprise | 10,000 | 15,000 | Unlimited |

Clients exceeding the rate limit will receive a 429 Too Many Requests response.
Retry after the duration specified in the Retry-After response header.

6. Changelog
**v3** (2023-02-10): Initial release of this API version.

7. Support
For API support, contact the Platform Engineering via the internal developer portal.
SLA for API support queries: 2 business days.
Breaking changes are announced at least 90 days before taking effect.

8. Revision History
| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v3.0 | 2023-02-10 | Platform Architect | Initial documentation release |

body:
Title: HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline – Architecture Overview
Design Doc ID: SYS-DES-001
System: HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline
Architecture Status: implemented
Primary Author: Platform Architect
Reviewers: Data Engineering Lead, Compliance Officer
Department: Platform Engineering
Effective Date: 2022-03-01
Version: 1.0
ADR IDs: ADR-HYD-001, ADR-HYD-002
Related Services: HYMonitor, HYID, HYDrive

1. Overview
HYTech Solutions requires a standardised, automated deployment pipeline that supports multiple deployment strategies (blue-green, canary, rolling) with integrated approval gates and rollback capabilities across all production environments.
This document describes the architecture of the HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline system at HYTech Solutions.
Target SLA: 99.9% uptime uptime with a maximum 1 hour recovery time.
Expected data volume: Handles up to 500 deployment events per day across all production environments..

2. Architecture
The HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline follows a microservices architecture.
The HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline uses a microservices architecture to meet the scalability and reliability requirements defined in this document.

Components in this system interact via direct database access.
All inter-service communication is authenticated and uses TLS 1.3 or higher.

3. Components
| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deployment Orchestrator | Manages deployment lifecycle state machine and step sequencing. | Artifact Registry, Gate Evaluator |
| Artifact Registry | Stores and versions build artifacts for all applications. | None |
| Gate Evaluator | Evaluates pre- and post-deployment conditions including metric thresholds and smoke tests. | HYMonitor |
| Traffic Manager | Controls traffic routing weights for canary and blue-green deployments. | Load Balancer |
| Rollback Manager | Executes rollback operations by restoring the previous deployment state. | Deployment Orchestrator, Traffic Manager |
| Notification Router | Sends deployment status notifications to configured channels. | None |

4. Data Flow
The HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline processes requests through the following flow:

1. Client sends request to Deployment Orchestrator.
2. Deployment Orchestrator validates and forwards to Artifact Registry.
3. Processed result is stored and returned to the caller.

5. Decision Records
The following Architecture Decision Records inform the design described in this document:

**ADR-HYD-001** — Use pipeline architecture for HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline
Decision: Adopted after evaluation of monolithic and distributed approaches.
Rationale: Aligns with HYTech scaling requirements and deployment tooling.

**ADR-HYD-002** — Select primary data store for HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline
Decision: PostgreSQL selected for transactional consistency.
Rationale: Meets ACID requirements and integrates with existing HYDataLake pipelines.


6. Failure Modes and Mitigations
The following failure modes have been identified and mitigated:

| Failure Mode | Impact | Mitigation | Residual Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gate evaluation timeout | Service degradation or data unavailability | Gates time out after 300 seconds and block the deployment; operator manual override is required. | Low after mitigation |
| Artifact registry unavailable | Service degradation or data unavailability | Deployments are queued for up to 15 minutes; if the registry remains unavailable, the deployment fails with error code HYD-503. | Low after mitigation |

7. Scalability and Performance
The HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline scales horizontally.
- Peak throughput: Handles up to 500 deployment events per day across all production environments
- P99 latency target: 50 ms
- Horizontal scaling: Supported via stateless service instances behind a load balancer

8. Security Considerations
All components adhere to the HYTech Solutions security baseline.
All inter-service communication is authenticated via HYID mTLS. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256.
Related security controls: HY-AC-01, HY-DP-01, HY-IR-01.

9. Related Documents
- API-DOC-014
- API-DOC-009

10. Revision History
| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0 | 2022-01-30 | Platform Architect | Initial draft |

The HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline follows a pipeline architecture.
The HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline uses a pipeline architecture to meet the scalability and reliability requirements defined in this document.

body:
Title: HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline – Decision Records and Failure Modes
Design Doc ID: SYS-DES-003
System: HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline
Architecture Status: implemented
Primary Author: Solutions Architect
Reviewers: Solutions Architect, Legal Counsel
Department: Platform Engineering
Effective Date: 2022-07-09
Version: 1.2
ADR IDs: ADR-HYD-001, ADR-HYD-002, ADR-HYD-003, ADR-HYD-004
Related Services: HYMonitor, HYID, HYDrive

1. Overview
HYTech Solutions requires a standardised, automated deployment pipeline that supports multiple deployment strategies (blue-green, canary, rolling) with integrated approval gates and rollback capabilities across all production environments.
This document describes the architecture of the HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline system at HYTech Solutions.
Target SLA: 99.9% uptime uptime with a maximum 1 hour recovery time.
Expected data volume: Handles up to 500 deployment events per day across all production environments..

2. Architecture
The HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline follows a pipeline architecture.
The HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline uses a pipeline architecture to meet the scalability and reliability requirements defined in this document.

Components in this system interact via gRPC.
All inter-service communication is authenticated and uses TLS 1.3 or higher.

3. Components
| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deployment Orchestrator | Manages deployment lifecycle state machine and step sequencing. | Artifact Registry, Gate Evaluator |
| Artifact Registry | Stores and versions build artifacts for all applications. | None |
| Gate Evaluator | Evaluates pre- and post-deployment conditions including metric thresholds and smoke tests. | HYMonitor |
| Traffic Manager | Controls traffic routing weights for canary and blue-green deployments. | Load Balancer |
| Rollback Manager | Executes rollback operations by restoring the previous deployment state. | Deployment Orchestrator, Traffic Manager |
| Notification Router | Sends deployment status notifications to configured channels. | None |

4. Data Flow
The HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline processes requests through the following flow:

1. Operator triggers the operation via the HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline API.
2. Request is authenticated through HYID.
3. State machine advances; gate conditions are evaluated.
4. Final state is committed and audit log is written.

5. Decision Records
The following Architecture Decision Records inform the design described in this document:

**ADR-HYD-001** — Use gateway architecture for HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline
Decision: Adopted after evaluation of monolithic and distributed approaches.
Rationale: Aligns with HYTech scaling requirements and deployment tooling.

**ADR-HYD-002** — Select primary data store for HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline
Decision: PostgreSQL selected for transactional consistency.
Rationale: Meets ACID requirements and integrates with existing HYDataLake pipelines.

**ADR-HYD-003** — Authentication strategy
Decision: Delegate authentication to HYID using service-to-service mTLS.
Rationale: Centralised identity management reduces security surface area.

**ADR-HYD-004** — Observability strategy
Decision: Use HYMonitor for all metrics and alerting.
Rationale: Standardised observability reduces operational overhead.


6. Failure Modes and Mitigations
The following failure modes have been identified and mitigated:

| Failure Mode | Impact | Mitigation | Residual Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gate evaluation timeout | Service degradation or data unavailability | Gates time out after 300 seconds and block the deployment; operator manual override is required. | Low after mitigation |
| Artifact registry unavailable | Service degradation or data unavailability | Deployments are queued for up to 15 minutes; if the registry remains unavailable, the deployment fails with error code HYD-503. | Low after mitigation |
| Traffic manager rollback failure | Service degradation or data unavailability | A secondary static routing configuration is applied; on-call engineer is paged immediately. | Low after mitigation |

7. Scalability and Performance
The HYDeploy Deployment Pipeline scales horizontally.
- Peak throughput: Handles up to 500 deployment events per day across all production environments
- P99 latency target: 50 ms
- Horizontal scaling: Supported via stateless service instances behind a load balancer

8. Security Considerations
All components adhere to the HYTech Solutions security baseline.
All inter-service communication is authenticated via HYID mTLS. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256.
Related security controls: HY-AC-01, HY-DP-01, HY-IR-01.

9. Related Documents

metadata.title: HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design – Architecture Overview

body:
Title: HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design – Architecture Overview
Design Doc ID: SYS-DES-004
System: HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design
Architecture Status: implemented
Primary Author: Engineering Manager
Reviewers: Legal Counsel, Data Engineering Lead
Department: Platform Engineering
Effective Date: 2022-09-12
Version: 1.0
ADR IDs: ADR-HYM-001, ADR-HYM-002
Related Services: HYID, HYDataLake, HYDrive

1. Overview
HYTech Solutions requires a scalable, low-latency metrics and log ingestion system capable of handling 500,000 events per second at peak load with less than 5 seconds end-to-end latency.
This document describes the architecture of the HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design system at HYTech Solutions.
Target SLA: 99.95% uptime for ingestion; 99.9% for query uptime with a maximum 1 hour recovery time.
Expected data volume: 500,000 events per second at peak; 5 PB total storage..

2. Architecture
The HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design follows a pipeline architecture.
The HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design uses a pipeline architecture to meet the scalability and reliability requirements defined in this document.

Components in this system interact via event streaming.
All inter-service communication is authenticated and uses TLS 1.3 or higher.

3. Components
| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ingest Gateway | Authenticates and validates incoming metric and log payloads. | HYID |
| Write Buffer | Buffers incoming events in memory before batch writes to storage. | None |
| Partition Router | Routes events to time-partitioned storage buckets based on timestamp and service label. | HYDataLake |
| Aggregation Engine | Computes rollup aggregations (1m, 5m, 1h, 1d) over raw time-series data. | Write Buffer |
| Alert Evaluator | Evaluates alert rule conditions against incoming metrics in near-real time. | Aggregation Engine |

4. Data Flow
The HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design processes requests through the following flow:

1. Client sends request to Ingest Gateway.
2. Ingest Gateway validates and forwards to Write Buffer.
3. Processed result is stored and returned to the caller.

5. Decision Records
The following Architecture Decision Records inform the design described in this document:

**ADR-HYM-001** — Use microservices architecture for HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design
Decision: Adopted after evaluation of monolithic and distributed approaches.
Rationale: Aligns with HYTech scaling requirements and deployment tooling.

**ADR-HYM-002** — Select primary data store for HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design
Decision: PostgreSQL selected for transactional consistency.
Rationale: Meets ACID requirements and integrates with existing HYDataLake pipelines.


6. Failure Modes and Mitigations
The following failure modes have been identified and mitigated:

| Failure Mode | Impact | Mitigation | Residual Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Write buffer overflow | Service degradation or data unavailability | Back-pressure signals are sent to producers; events are dropped with error code HYM-503 if the buffer remains full for more than 30 seconds. | Low after mitigation |
| Partition router failure | Service degradation or data unavailability | Events are routed to a fallback partition; manual rebalancing is required after recovery. | Low after mitigation |

7. Scalability and Performance
The HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design scales horizontally.
- Peak throughput: 500,000 events per second at peak; 5 PB total storage
- P99 latency target: 100 ms
- Horizontal scaling: Supported via stateless service instances behind a load balancer

8. Security Considerations
All components adhere to the HYTech Solutions security baseline.
All inter-service communication is authenticated via HYID mTLS. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256.
Related security controls: HY-AC-01, HY-DP-01, HY-IR-01.

9. Related Documents
- API-DOC-011
- API-DOC-015

| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

HYTech Solutions requires a scalable, low-latency metrics and log ingestion system capable of handling 500,000 events per second at peak load with less than 5 seconds end-to-end latency.
This document describes the architecture of the HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design system at HYTech Solutions.
Target SLA: 99.95% uptime for ingestion; 99.9% for query uptime with a maximum 1 hour recovery time.
Expected data volume: 500,000 events per second at peak; 5 PB total storage..

2. Architecture
The HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design follows a microservices architecture.
The HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design uses a microservices architecture to meet the scalability and reliability requirements defined in this document.

Components in this system interact via message queues.
All inter-service communication is authenticated and uses TLS 1.3 or higher.

3. Components
| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ingest Gateway | Authenticates and validates incoming metric and log payloads. | HYID |
| Write Buffer | Buffers incoming events in memory before batch writes to storage. | None |
| Partition Router | Routes events to time-partitioned storage buckets based on timestamp and service label. | HYDataLake |
| Aggregation Engine | Computes rollup aggregations (1m, 5m, 1h, 1d) over raw time-series data. | Write Buffer |
| Alert Evaluator | Evaluates alert rule conditions against incoming metrics in near-real time. | Aggregation Engine |

4. Data Flow
The HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design processes requests through the following flow:

1. Incoming event arrives at Ingest Gateway.
2. Event is validated, enriched, and routed based on type.
3. Result is persisted and a completion notification is emitted.
4. Monitoring metrics are published to HYMonitor.

5. Decision Records
The following Architecture Decision Records inform the design described in this document:

**ADR-HYM-001** — Use layered architecture for HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design
Decision: Adopted after evaluation of monolithic and distributed approaches.
Rationale: Aligns with HYTech scaling requirements and deployment tooling.

**ADR-HYM-002** — Select primary data store for HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design
Decision: PostgreSQL selected for transactional consistency.
Rationale: Meets ACID requirements and integrates with existing HYDataLake pipelines.

**ADR-HYM-003** — Authentication strategy
Decision: Delegate authentication to HYID using service-to-service mTLS.
Rationale: Centralised identity management reduces security surface area.

| Alert evaluator lag | Service degradation or data unavailability | Alerts are delayed but not lost; a lag threshold of 60 seconds triggers an operational alert. | Low after mitigation |

HYTech Solutions requires a scalable, low-latency metrics and log ingestion system capable of handling 500,000 events per second at peak load with less than 5 seconds end-to-end latency.
This document describes the architecture of the HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design system at HYTech Solutions.
Target SLA: 99.95% uptime for ingestion; 99.9% for query uptime with a maximum 1 hour recovery time.
Expected data volume: 500,000 events per second at peak; 5 PB total storage..

2. Architecture
The HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design follows a gateway architecture.
The HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design uses a gateway architecture to meet the scalability and reliability requirements defined in this document.

Components in this system interact via event streaming.
All inter-service communication is authenticated and uses TLS 1.3 or higher.

3. Components
| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ingest Gateway | Authenticates and validates incoming metric and log payloads. | HYID |
| Write Buffer | Buffers incoming events in memory before batch writes to storage. | None |
| Partition Router | Routes events to time-partitioned storage buckets based on timestamp and service label. | HYDataLake |
| Aggregation Engine | Computes rollup aggregations (1m, 5m, 1h, 1d) over raw time-series data. | Write Buffer |
| Alert Evaluator | Evaluates alert rule conditions against incoming metrics in near-real time. | Aggregation Engine |

4. Data Flow
The HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design processes requests through the following flow:

1. Operator triggers the operation via the HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design API.
2. Request is authenticated through HYID.
3. State machine advances; gate conditions are evaluated.
4. Final state is committed and audit log is written.

5. Decision Records
The following Architecture Decision Records inform the design described in this document:

**ADR-HYM-001** — Use event-driven architecture for HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design
Decision: Adopted after evaluation of monolithic and distributed approaches.
Rationale: Aligns with HYTech scaling requirements and deployment tooling.

**ADR-HYM-002** — Select primary data store for HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design
Decision: PostgreSQL selected for transactional consistency.
Rationale: Meets ACID requirements and integrates with existing HYDataLake pipelines.

**ADR-HYM-003** — Authentication strategy
Decision: Delegate authentication to HYID using service-to-service mTLS.
Rationale: Centralised identity management reduces security surface area.

**ADR-HYM-004** — Observability strategy
Decision: Use HYMonitor for all metrics and alerting.
Rationale: Standardised observability reduces operational overhead.


6. Failure Modes and Mitigations
The following failure modes have been identified and mitigated:

| Failure Mode | Impact | Mitigation | Residual Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Write buffer overflow | Service degradation or data unavailability | Back-pressure signals are sent to producers; events are dropped with error code HYM-503 if the buffer remains full for more than 30 seconds. | Low after mitigation |
| Partition router failure | Service degradation or data unavailability | Events are routed to a fallback partition; manual rebalancing is required after recovery. | Low after mitigation |
| Alert evaluator lag | Service degradation or data unavailability | Alerts are delayed but not lost; a lag threshold of 60 seconds triggers an operational alert. | Low after mitigation |

7. Scalability and Performance
The HYMonitor Event Ingestion Design scales horizontally.
- Peak throughput: 500,000 events per second at peak; 5 PB total storage
- P99 latency target: 500 ms
- Horizontal scaling: Supported via stateless service instances behind a load balancer

8. Security Considerations
All components adhere to the HYTech Solutions security baseline.
All inter-service communication is authenticated via HYID mTLS. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256.
Related security controls: HY-AC-01, HY-DP-01, HY-IR-01.

9. Related Documents

- API-DOC-017

| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| 1.2 | 2023-01-20 | Platform Architect | Added decision records and failure modes section |

Title: HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture – Architecture Overview

1. Overview
The HYDataLake must support petabyte-scale storage with efficient partitioning for both analytical workloads and operational data pipelines, while maintaining data lineage and schema evolution capabilities.
This document describes the architecture of the HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture system at HYTech Solutions.
Target SLA: 99.9% uptime for read; 99.5% for write uptime with a maximum 1 hour recovery time.
Expected data volume: Current storage: 5 PB. Expected growth: 2 PB per year..

2. Architecture
The HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture follows a pipeline architecture.
The HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture uses a pipeline architecture to meet the scalability and reliability requirements defined in this document.

Components in this system interact via gRPC.
All inter-service communication is authenticated and uses TLS 1.3 or higher.

3. Components
| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Schema Registry | Stores and versions dataset schemas; validates incoming data against registered schemas. | None |
| Partition Manager | Creates and maintains partition metadata; routes data to correct partition paths. | Schema Registry |
| Lineage Tracker | Records data transformation history and dependencies. | None |
| Compaction Service | Merges small files into optimal Parquet files to reduce query overhead. | Partition Manager |
| Time-Travel Store | Maintains snapshots for point-in-time query support. | Partition Manager |
| Access Controller | Enforces column-level and row-level access policies. | HYID |

4. Data Flow
The HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture processes requests through the following flow:

1. Client sends request to Schema Registry.
2. Schema Registry validates and forwards to Partition Manager.
3. Processed result is stored and returned to the caller.

5. Decision Records
The following Architecture Decision Records inform the design described in this document:

**ADR-HDL-001** — Use microservices architecture for HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture
Decision: Adopted after evaluation of monolithic and distributed approaches.
Rationale: Aligns with HYTech scaling requirements and deployment tooling.

**ADR-HDL-002** — Select primary data store for HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture
Decision: PostgreSQL selected for transactional consistency.
Rationale: Meets ACID requirements and integrates with existing HYDataLake pipelines.


6. Failure Modes and Mitigations
The following failure modes have been identified and mitigated:

| Failure Mode | Impact | Mitigation | Residual Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compaction service backlog | Service degradation or data unavailability | Read performance degrades gracefully; compaction is prioritised during off-peak hours. | Low after mitigation |
| Schema registry unavailable | Service degradation or data unavailability | Ingestion is paused; buffered events are retried for up to 30 minutes. | Low after mitigation |

7. Scalability and Performance
The HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture scales horizontally.
- Peak throughput: Current storage: 5 PB
- P99 latency target: 500 ms
- Horizontal scaling: Supported via stateless service instances behind a load balancer

8. Security Considerations
All components adhere to the HYTech Solutions security baseline.
All inter-service communication is authenticated via HYID mTLS. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256.
Related security controls: HY-AC-01, HY-DP-01, HY-IR-01.

The HYDataLake must support petabyte-scale storage with efficient partitioning for both analytical workloads and operational data pipelines, while maintaining data lineage and schema evolution capabilities.
This document describes the architecture of the HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture system at HYTech Solutions.
Target SLA: 99.9% uptime for read; 99.5% for write uptime with a maximum 1 hour recovery time.
Expected data volume: Current storage: 5 PB. Expected growth: 2 PB per year..

2. Architecture
The HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture follows a layered architecture.
The HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture uses a layered architecture to meet the scalability and reliability requirements defined in this document.

Components in this system interact via gRPC.
All inter-service communication is authenticated and uses TLS 1.3 or higher.

3. Components
| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Schema Registry | Stores and versions dataset schemas; validates incoming data against registered schemas. | None |
| Partition Manager | Creates and maintains partition metadata; routes data to correct partition paths. | Schema Registry |
| Lineage Tracker | Records data transformation history and dependencies. | None |
| Compaction Service | Merges small files into optimal Parquet files to reduce query overhead. | Partition Manager |
| Time-Travel Store | Maintains snapshots for point-in-time query support. | Partition Manager |
| Access Controller | Enforces column-level and row-level access policies. | HYID |

4. Data Flow
The HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture processes requests through the following flow:

1. Incoming event arrives at Schema Registry.
2. Event is validated, enriched, and routed based on type.
3. Result is persisted and a completion notification is emitted.
4. Monitoring metrics are published to HYMonitor.

5. Decision Records
The following Architecture Decision Records inform the design described in this document:

**ADR-HDL-001** — Use event-driven architecture for HYDataLake Partitioning Architecture
Decision: Adopted after evaluation of monolithic and distributed approaches.

Rationale: Meets ACID requirements and integrates with existing HYDataLake pipelines.

**ADR-HDL-003** — Authentication strategy
Decision: Delegate authentication to HYID using service-to-service mTLS.
Rationale: Centralised identity management reduces security surface area.

| Failure Mode | Impact | Mitigation | Residual Risk |

Title: HYID Authentication Architecture – Architecture Overview
Design Doc ID: SYS-DES-010
System: HYID Authentication Architecture
Architecture Status: implemented
Primary Author: Product Manager
Reviewers: Data Engineering Lead, Site Reliability Engineer
Department: Platform Engineering
Effective Date: 2023-10-07
Version: 1.0
ADR IDs: ADR-HYID-001, ADR-HYID-002
Related Services: HYDataLake, HYMonitor, HYVault

1. Overview
HYTech Solutions requires a centralised, standards-compliant identity and access management system that supports OAuth2, SAML 2.0, and service-to-service authentication for over 1,200 employees and 50 internal services.
This document describes the architecture of the HYID Authentication Architecture system at HYTech Solutions.
Target SLA: 99.99% uptime for token validation; 99.9% for token issuance uptime with a maximum 1 hour recovery time.
Expected data volume: Issues up to 50,000 tokens per minute at peak..

2. Architecture
The HYID Authentication Architecture follows a layered architecture.
The HYID Authentication Architecture uses a layered architecture to meet the scalability and reliability requirements defined in this document.

Components in this system interact via direct database access.
All inter-service communication is authenticated and uses TLS 1.3 or higher.

3. Components
| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token Issuer | Issues JWT access tokens and refresh tokens after successful authentication. | User Directory, Key Manager |
| User Directory | Stores user profiles, credentials, and group memberships. | None |
| Key Manager | Manages signing keys for JWT tokens; rotates keys on a 90-day schedule. | HYVault |
| SAML Bridge | Translates SAML 2.0 assertions to HYID tokens for federated identity providers. | Token Issuer |
| Session Manager | Tracks active sessions and handles logout and forced revocation. | User Directory |
| Audit Logger | Records all authentication events to HYDataLake for security auditing. | HYDataLake |

4. Data Flow
The HYID Authentication Architecture processes requests through the following flow:

1. Client sends request to Token Issuer.
2. Token Issuer validates and forwards to User Directory.
3. Processed result is stored and returned to the caller.

5. Decision Records
The following Architecture Decision Records inform the design described in this document:

**ADR-HYID-001** — Use pipeline architecture for HYID Authentication Architecture
Decision: Adopted after evaluation of monolithic and distributed approaches.
Rationale: Aligns with HYTech scaling requirements and deployment tooling.

**ADR-HYID-002** — Select primary data store for HYID Authentication Architecture
Decision: PostgreSQL selected for transactional consistency.
Rationale: Meets ACID requirements and integrates with existing HYDataLake pipelines.


6. Failure Modes and Mitigations
The following failure modes have been identified and mitigated:

| Failure Mode | Impact | Mitigation | Residual Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Key manager unavailable | Service degradation or data unavailability | Token issuance fails; existing tokens remain valid until expiry. Key Manager has a 3-node HA deployment. | Low after mitigation |
| User directory replication lag | Service degradation or data unavailability | Read replicas may serve stale data; write-through caching reduces but does not eliminate the risk. | Low after mitigation |

7. Scalability and Performance
The HYID Authentication Architecture scales horizontally.
- Peak throughput: Issues up to 50,000 tokens per minute at peak
- P99 latency target: 500 ms
- Horizontal scaling: Supported via stateless service instances behind a load balancer

8. Security Considerations
All components adhere to the HYTech Solutions security baseline.
All inter-service communication is authenticated via HYID mTLS. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256.
Related security controls: HY-AC-01, HY-DP-01, HY-IR-01.

9. Related Documents
- API-DOC-006
- API-DOC-001

10. Revision History
| Version | Date | Author Role | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0 | 2023-09-07 | Product Manager | Initial draft |

2. Architecture
The HYID Authentication Architecture follows a microservices architecture.
The HYID Authentication Architecture uses a microservices architecture to meet the scalability and reliability requirements defined in this document.

Components in this system interact via message queues.
All inter-service communication is authenticated and uses TLS 1.3 or higher.

3. Components
| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |

Title: Notification Routing Design – Architecture Overview
Design Doc ID: SYS-DES-012
System: Notification Routing Design
Architecture Status: proposed
Primary Author: Platform Architect
Reviewers: DevOps Engineer, Legal Counsel
Department: Platform Engineering
Effective Date: 2024-02-14
Version: 1.0
ADR IDs: ADR-NTF-001, ADR-NTF-002
Related Services: HYID, HYMonitor

1. Overview
HYTech Solutions internal services require a unified notification routing layer that can deliver alerts and status updates to multiple channels (email, Slack, PagerDuty) with guaranteed at-least-once delivery and deduplication.
This document describes the architecture of the Notification Routing Design system at HYTech Solutions.
Target SLA: 99.9% delivery rate; 10-second delivery latency at p95 uptime with a maximum 1 hour recovery time.
Expected data volume: Up to 10,000 notifications per hour during peak incident periods..

2. Architecture
The Notification Routing Design follows a layered architecture.
The Notification Routing Design uses a layered architecture to meet the scalability and reliability requirements defined in this document.

Components in this system interact via REST APIs.
All inter-service communication is authenticated and uses TLS 1.3 or higher.

3. Components
| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Notification Gateway | Accepts notification requests from internal services and validates the payload. | HYID |
| Deduplication Store | Stores idempotency keys to prevent duplicate delivery within a 24-hour window. | None |
| Channel Router | Routes notifications to the appropriate channel adapter based on the configured routing rules. | Deduplication Store |
| Email Adapter | Formats and delivers email notifications via the corporate SMTP gateway. | None |
| Slack Adapter | Delivers formatted messages to Slack channels via the Slack Web API. | None |
| PagerDuty Adapter | Creates and resolves PagerDuty incidents for on-call alerts. | None |

4. Data Flow
The Notification Routing Design processes requests through the following flow:

1. Client sends request to Notification Gateway.
2. Notification Gateway validates and forwards to Deduplication Store.
3. Processed result is stored and returned to the caller.

5. Decision Records
The following Architecture Decision Records inform the design described in this document:

**ADR-NTF-001** — Use microservices architecture for Notification Routing Design
Decision: Adopted after evaluation of monolithic and distributed approaches.
Rationale: Aligns with HYTech scaling requirements and deployment tooling.

**ADR-NTF-002** — Select primary data store for Notification Routing Design
Decision: PostgreSQL selected for transactional consistency.
Rationale: Meets ACID requirements and integrates with existing HYDataLake pipelines.


6. Failure Modes and Mitigations
The following failure modes have been identified and mitigated:

| Failure Mode | Impact | Mitigation | Residual Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Channel adapter timeout | Service degradation or data unavailability | Failed deliveries are retried with exponential backoff up to 5 times; undelivered notifications are moved to a dead-letter queue. | Low after mitigation |
| Deduplication store unavailable | Service degradation or data unavailability | Deduplication is bypassed; duplicate notifications may be delivered. An alert is raised for manual review. | Low after mitigation |

7. Scalability and Performance
The Notification Routing Design scales horizontally.
- Peak throughput: Up to 10,000 notifications per hour during peak incident periods
- P99 latency target: 200 ms
- Horizontal scaling: Supported via stateless service instances behind a load balancer

8. Security Considerations
All components adhere to the HYTech Solutions security baseline.
All inter-service communication is authenticated via HYID mTLS. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256.
Related security controls: HY-AC-01, HY-DP-01, HY-IR-01.

- API-DOC-004
